map.state: SOFI 2026 nowcasts 645 million people undernourished in 2025 (7.8%); 266 million in 47 food-crisis countries faced high acute food insecurity in 2025. On 27 November 2026 FAO and WFP named 16 hunger hotspots for December 2026 to May 2027, up from 13 in June.
map.compared_with: 658.8 million (8.1%) in 2024 (SOFI 2026, Tables 2.1 and 2.2, same revised series). 2025 is a nowcast, and SOFI says it may not fully reflect the worsening situation in humanitarian crises. The acute figure has no like comparison: 296 million in 53 countries in 2024, and the GRFC says the fall mainly reflects fewer countries covered. Its analysed share was 22.7% in 2024. Mid-year Update, data to 31 August 2026: of 33 comparable countries and territories 17 improved, 15 worsened. The 17 include DR Congo (26.5 million against 27.7 million at the 2025 peak), on an analysis that did not yet consider Ebola; the IPC analysis released on 30 October 2026 has since put it at 28.8 million for September to December 2026. Hunger Hotspots, 27 November 2026: 16 hotspots against 13 in the June 2026 edition; a hotspot is a place where acute food insecurity is expected to deteriorate significantly over the outlook period, chosen by consensus, not a count of people, so the number of hotspots is no measure of how many go hungry.

map.state: October 2026 was the warmest October in Copernicus's ERA5 record, 1.75°C above pre-industrial, the third month in a row above 1.5°C; the 12 months to it stood at 1.51°C. A Copernicus statistical model puts 2026 at 1.56–1.61°C, virtually certain above 1.5°C.

matters.title: Losses of control, and who must answer
matters.gist: Britain kept a power over essential services whose AI agents slip out of control, Brussels had to ask two AI makers twice for a full account of their incidents, and an Australian committee asked for reporting deadlines.

lines.text: On 24 November the UK Commons agreed a power to make rules where an essential service is compromised through loss of oversight or control of an AI agent; how it will work is left to consultation.
lines.say: On the twenty-fourth of November the UK Commons agreed a power to make rules where an essential service is compromised through loss of oversight or control of an AI agent; how it will work is left to consultation.

lines.text: The Commons voted 278 to 93 against writing ‘autonomous system’ for ‘AI agent’, and refused a Lords review of powers for the AI Security Institute; the Lords return to it on 7 December.
lines.say: The Commons voted two hundred and seventy-eight to ninety-three against writing autonomous system for AI agent, and refused a Lords review of powers for the AI Security Institute; the Lords return to it on the seventh of December.

lines.text: On 25 November the European Commission said OpenAI and Anthropic had each answered two requests on their incidents, the latest on 24 November, and that it would not make the numbers public.
lines.say: On the twenty-fifth of November the European Commission said OpenAI and Anthropic had each answered two requests on their incidents, the latest on the twenty-fourth of November, and that it would not make the numbers public.

lines.text: On 24 November an Australian parliamentary committee recommended that frontier labs be required to monitor and report incidents to the government, with clear reporting deadlines.
lines.say: On the twenty-fourth of November an Australian parliamentary committee recommended that frontier labs be required to monitor and report incidents to the government, with clear reporting deadlines.

lines.text: California's suit of 16 November says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents over 80 times in testing and had publicly reported 27 such incidents; nothing is decided.
lines.say: California's suit of the sixteenth of November says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents over eighty times in testing and had publicly reported twenty-seven such incidents; nothing is decided.

matters.title: Appeals less than half funded
matters.gist: With a month of the year left, the world's humanitarian appeals have received less than half of what they asked for, and next year's appeal is not yet out.

lines.text: On 28 November, the 2026 humanitarian appeals had received 15.90 of 35.06 billion dollars, 45.4 percent.
lines.say: On the twenty-eighth of November, the twenty twenty-six humanitarian appeals had received fifteen point nine of thirty-five point zero six billion dollars, forty-five point four percent.

lines.text: Niger's plan was 20.0 percent funded and Yemen's 23.0; the flash appeal for Honduras had 3.5 percent.
lines.say: Niger's plan was twenty percent funded and Yemen's twenty-three; the flash appeal for Honduras had three point five percent.

lines.text: Sudan's plan, for the world's largest forced displacement situation, stood at 50.9 percent.
lines.say: Sudan's plan, for the world's largest forced displacement situation, stood at fifty point nine percent.

lines.text: The United States gave 30.7 percent of the money these appeals received.
lines.say: The United States gave thirty point seven percent of the money these appeals received.

lines.text: On 26 November NRC said 321,000 people had been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated in August.
lines.say: On the twenty-sixth of November the Norwegian Refugee Council said three hundred and twenty-one thousand people had been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated in August.

lines.text: At the end of June 2026, by UNHCR's estimate, 118.2 million people were forcibly displaced, one in every 70 on Earth.
lines.say: At the end of June twenty twenty-six, by the UN refugee agency's estimate, one hundred and eighteen point two million people were forcibly displaced, one in every seventy on Earth.

matters.title: One in ten below three dollars a day
matters.gist: Extreme poverty barely moves: about one in ten people live on less than three dollars a day, and a wider measure finds more than one in six poor in the 108 countries it covers.

lines.text: The World Bank counts 824 million people below three dollars a day in 2024, the latest year with sufficient data.
lines.say: The World Bank counts eight hundred and twenty-four million people below three dollars a day in twenty twenty-four, the latest year with sufficient data.

lines.text: Its nowcast for 2026 is about 811 million, one in ten.
lines.say: Its now cast for twenty twenty-six is about eight hundred and eleven million, one in ten.

lines.text: In their 2026 update, UNDP and OPHI count 1.2 billion people in acute multidimensional poverty in 108 countries.
lines.say: In their twenty twenty-six update, the United Nations Development Programme and Oxford's poverty initiative count one point two billion people in acute multidimensional poverty in one hundred and eight countries.

lines.text: From 1990 to 2026 average consumption worldwide rose about 70 percent, that of people remaining in extreme poverty about 10 percent, by World Bank estimates.
lines.say: From nineteen ninety to twenty twenty-six average consumption worldwide rose about seventy percent, that of people remaining in extreme poverty about ten percent, by World Bank estimates.

matters.title: Killed by those closest to them
matters.gist: Most women and girls who are killed intentionally die at the hands of a partner or a relative, and in the Americas and Europe that rate falls more slowly than homicide overall.

lines.text: UNODC and UN Women estimate that around 47,000 women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member in 2025, in a range of 37,100 to 56,700.
lines.say: UNODC and UN Women estimate that around forty-seven thousand women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member in twenty twenty-five, in a range of thirty-seven thousand one hundred to fifty-six thousand seven hundred.

lines.text: That is almost 60 percent of the women and girls killed intentionally that year; for men and boys the share is 11 percent.
lines.say: That is almost sixty percent of the women and girls killed intentionally that year; for men and boys the share is eleven percent.

lines.text: The authors say the drop from 50,000 in 2024 largely reflects better data and is no evidence of a decline.
lines.say: The authors say the drop from fifty thousand in twenty twenty-four largely reflects better data and is no evidence of a decline.

lines.text: In the Americas and Europe the rate fell between 2010 and 2025 more slowly than homicide as a whole.
lines.say: In the Americas and Europe the rate fell between twenty ten and twenty twenty-five more slowly than homicide as a whole.

matters.title: Six in seven journalist killings unpunished
matters.gist: Most killings of journalists are never brought to justice, and the share left unresolved has risen for the first time since UNESCO began measuring it.

lines.text: UNESCO verified 189 killings of journalists, media workers and social media producers in 2024 and 2025, 20 percent more than in the two years before.
lines.say: UNESCO verified one hundred and eighty-nine killings of journalists, media workers and social media producers in twenty twenty-four and twenty twenty-five, twenty percent more than in the two years before.

lines.text: 127 of them, two thirds, were killed in countries in armed conflict, and 50 by drones.
lines.say: One hundred and twenty-seven of them, two thirds, were killed in countries in armed conflict, and fifty by drones.

lines.text: In 2026 the share of killings since 2006 left unresolved rose to 86 percent, the first rise since UNESCO began measuring it in 2012.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-six the share of killings since two thousand and six left unresolved rose to eighty-six percent, the first rise since UNESCO began measuring it in twenty twelve.

lines.text: Between 18 and 23 November 2026 UNESCO's Director-General condemned killings of journalists in Ecuador, Mexico, Costa Rica and Ukraine.
lines.say: Between the eighteenth and the twenty-third of November twenty twenty-six, UNESCO's Director-General condemned killings of journalists in Ecuador, Mexico, Costa Rica and Ukraine.

lines.text: RSF's 2026 index rates press freedom difficult or very serious in 52.2 percent of 180 countries and territories, against 13.7 percent in 2002.
lines.say: The twenty twenty-six index of Reporters Without Borders rates press freedom difficult or very serious in fifty-two point two percent of one hundred and eighty countries and territories, against thirteen point seven percent in two thousand and two.

matters.title: Sixteen hotspots where hunger is expected to worsen
matters.gist: FAO and WFP expect acute hunger to worsen in sixteen hotspots over the next six months, with El Niño adding new ones, while aid to the worst of them has shrunk.

lines.text: On 27 November 2026 FAO and WFP named 16 hunger hotspots where acute food insecurity is expected to worsen from December 2026 to May 2027, up from 13 in June.
lines.say: On the twenty-seventh of November twenty twenty-six the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme named sixteen hunger hotspots where acute food insecurity is expected to worsen from December twenty twenty-six to May twenty twenty-seven, up from thirteen in June.

lines.text: Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen are of highest concern; in four of the five, analyses found or projected people in Catastrophe.
lines.say: Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen are of highest concern; in four of the five, analyses found or projected people in Catastrophe.

lines.text: In Sudan a risk of Famine is projected in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January 2027, under a reasonable worst-case scenario.
lines.say: In Sudan a risk of Famine is projected in thirteen areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January twenty twenty-seven, under a reasonable worst-case scenario.

lines.text: Aid for food security and nutrition in those five fell about 62 percent, from 5.1 billion dollars in 2022 to 2.0 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Aid for food security and nutrition in those five fell about sixty-two percent, from five point one billion dollars in twenty twenty-two to two billion in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In DR Congo a record 30.3 million people are projected to face Crisis or worse from January to June 2027.
lines.say: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo a record thirty point three million people are projected to face Crisis or worse from January to June twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: On 25 November the IPC said the risk of Famine among displaced people in Baidoa, Somalia, is no longer expected through December 2026.
lines.say: On the twenty-fifth of November the IPC said the risk of Famine among displaced people in Baidoa, Somalia, is no longer expected through December twenty twenty-six.

matters.title: Extinction risk, before the Red List's next update
matters.gist: IUCN still plans its next Red List update for 3 December; the index that follows extinction risk in five well-assessed groups has kept declining since 1993.

lines.text: IUCN's schedule still names 3 December 2026 for the next Red List update, version 2026-2, and says the date may change.
lines.say: IUCN's schedule still names the third of December twenty twenty-six for the next Red List update, version twenty twenty-six dash two, and says the date may change.

lines.text: The July 2026 Red List counts 49,505 threatened species among 175,909 assessed, a count that grows as more species are assessed.
lines.say: The July twenty twenty-six Red List counts forty-nine thousand, five hundred and five threatened species among one hundred and seventy-five thousand, nine hundred and nine assessed, a count that grows as more species are assessed.

lines.text: The Red List Index for mammals, birds, amphibians, corals and cycads, modelled between assessments, fell from 0.806 in 1993 to 0.745 in 2025.
lines.say: The Red List Index for mammals, birds, amphibians, corals and cycads, modelled between assessments, fell from zero point eight zero six in nineteen ninety-three to zero point seven four five in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In July, IUCN found 62 percent of endemic hydrothermal-vent molluscs at risk of extinction from deep-sea mining.
lines.say: In July, IUCN found sixty-two percent of endemic hydrothermal-vent molluscs at risk of extinction from deep-sea mining.

matters.title: Civic space under pressure in every region
matters.gist: The UN Human Rights Office finds the room to speak, organise and protest narrowing in every region.

lines.text: By data the UN Human Rights Office compiled, at least 5,995 human rights defenders, journalists and trade unionists were killed or forcibly disappeared between 2015 and 2025.
lines.say: By data the UN Human Rights Office compiled, at least five thousand nine hundred and ninety-five human rights defenders, journalists and trade unionists were killed or forcibly disappeared between twenty fifteen and twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: 813 of them, 13 percent, were women; the Office calls its count the tip of the iceberg.
lines.say: Eight hundred and thirteen of them, thirteen percent, were women; the Office calls its count the tip of the iceberg.

lines.text: The report cites CIVICUS's 2025 update: only 7 percent of the world's people lived in countries with free or relatively open civic space.
lines.say: The report cites the twenty twenty-five update of CIVICUS: only seven percent of the world's people lived in countries with free or relatively open civic space.

lines.text: Authorities reportedly intervened in at least 30,900 demonstrations between January 2023 and July 2026, an AI-coded count of media reports that shows trends, not verified numbers.
lines.say: Authorities reportedly intervened in at least thirty thousand nine hundred demonstrations between January twenty twenty-three and July twenty twenty-six, an AI-coded count of media reports that shows trends, not verified numbers.

lines.text: More than 80 percent of civil society respondents to its survey said their space had narrowed; over 70 percent of respondents said funding had fallen sharply or stopped.
lines.say: More than eighty percent of civil society respondents to its survey said their space had narrowed; over seventy percent of respondents said funding had fallen sharply or stopped.

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and the US now requires a licence to rent large amounts of it abroad to firms from countries it embargoes.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held 71 percent of the world's AI compute at the end of 2025, on incomplete records of who owns chips.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held seventy-one percent of the world's AI compute at the end of twenty twenty-five, on incomplete records of who owns chips.

lines.text: Since 19 November a US rule requires a licence for chips with which a data centre anywhere would give large amounts of compute to firms from Macau or US arms-embargoed countries such as China.
lines.say: Since the nineteenth of November a US rule requires a licence for chips with which a data centre anywhere would give large amounts of compute to firms from Macau or US arms-embargoed countries such as China.

lines.text: It also requires licences for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, except to firms based in the US or with a US parent, if the exporter files monthly reports.
On 23 November the US put seven firms in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, among them Megaspeed International, on its Entity List over the risk of diverting advanced chips.
lines.say: On the twenty-third of November the US put seven firms in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, among them Megaspeed International, on its Entity List over the risk of diverting advanced chips.

lines.text: Licences to supply them will be reviewed with a presumption of denial; Malaysia said on 24 November it would advise every data-centre operator not to host or serve the seven.
lines.say: Licences to supply them will be reviewed with a presumption of denial; Malaysia said on the twenty-fourth of November it would advise every data-centre operator not to host or serve the seven.

lines.text: China called the remote-access rule economic coercion and said it would take countermeasures if the US persisted; comments are open until 19 January 2027.
lines.say: China called the remote-access rule economic coercion and said it would take countermeasures if the US persisted; comments are open until the nineteenth of January twenty twenty-seven.

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo still adds dozens of confirmed cases a day, more of them now in Nord-Kivu than in Ituri.

lines.text: By 26 November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at 12,176 confirmed cases, including 5,978 deaths.
lines.say: By the twenty-sixth of November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at twelve thousand, one hundred and seventy-six confirmed cases, including five thousand, nine hundred and seventy-eight deaths.

lines.text: On 26 November alone it added 87 confirmed cases, 54 of them in Nord-Kivu, and 35 confirmed deaths, 25 in the community.
lines.say: On the twenty-sixth of November alone it added eighty-seven confirmed cases, fifty-four of them in Nord-Kivu, and thirty-five confirmed deaths, twenty-five in the community.

lines.text: From 21 to 26 November Nord-Kivu added 216 confirmed cases and Ituri 159.
lines.say: From the twenty-first to the twenty-sixth of November Nord-Kivu added two hundred and sixteen confirmed cases and Ituri one hundred and fifty-nine.

lines.text: Contact follow-up fell to 79.2 percent on 26 November, below the 95 percent threshold.
lines.say: Contact follow-up fell to seventy-nine point two percent on the twenty-sixth of November, below the ninety-five percent threshold.

lines.text: On 25 November WHO's chief issued updated recommendations for the outbreak, which remains a public health emergency of international concern.
lines.say: On the twenty-fifth of November the head of the World Health Organization issued updated recommendations for the outbreak, which remains a public health emergency of international concern.

lines.text: WHO has verified at least 94 attacks on health care in Congo since the emergency was declared six months ago.
lines.say: The World Health Organization has verified at least ninety-four attacks on health care in Congo since the emergency was declared six months ago.

matters.title: COP31's cover decisions stay unadopted
matters.gist: A week after the climate summit in Antalya closed without its overarching decisions, no resumed session has been announced.

lines.text: COP31 in Antalya ended on 22 November 2026, almost 50 hours late, without adopting its two cover decisions, together the Antalya Pact.
lines.say: COP thirty-one in Antalya ended on the twenty-second of November twenty twenty-six, almost fifty hours late, without adopting its two cover decisions, together the Antalya Pact.

lines.text: Parties also rejected draft decisions on the mitigation work programme, on response measures and on guidance to the Global Environment Facility.
With no decision adopted on the mitigation work programme, its future is now unclear, the Earth Negotiations Bulletin wrote on 24 November.
lines.say: With no decision adopted on the mitigation work programme, its future is now unclear, the Earth Negotiations Bulletin wrote on the twenty-fourth of November.

lines.text: By 28 November no resumed session on the pact had been announced; the next steps are the June 2027 sessions and COP32 in Addis Ababa, 8 to 19 November 2027.
lines.say: By the twenty-eighth of November no resumed session on the pact had been announced; the next steps are the sessions of June twenty twenty-seven and COP thirty-two in Addis Ababa, from the eighth to the nineteenth of November twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: UNEP finds that current policies could take warming to 2.8°C this century.
lines.say: The UN Environment Programme finds that current policies could take warming to two point eight degrees this century.

lines.text: WMO puts January to September 2026 at about 1.47°C above pre-industrial.
lines.say: The World Meteorological Organization puts January to September twenty twenty-six at about one point four seven degrees above pre-industrial.
